definitions.explanation: Vinegar that has been blended with other seasonings such as sugar, salt, soy sauce, or dashi. Used as a base for various Japanese dishes including sushi rice, vinegared dishes (sunomono), and dressings.

examples.japanese: {合|あ}わせ{酢|ず}を{作|つく}っておく。
examples.english: Prepare the seasoned vinegar in advance.

examples.japanese: {酢|す}の{物|もの}には{合|あ}わせ{酢|ず}をかける。
examples.english: Pour seasoned vinegar over the vinegared dishes.

examples.japanese: {寿司|すし}{酢|ず}は{酢|す}と{砂糖|さとう}と{塩|しお}を{混|ま}ぜた{合|あ}わせ{酢|ず}の{一種|いっしゅ}だ。
examples.english: Sushi vinegar is a type of seasoned vinegar made by mixing vinegar with sugar and salt.

notes:
USAGE:
A cooking term. {合|あ}わせ means "combined" and {酢|ず} (voiced form of {酢|す}) means "vinegar." The voicing of す to ず occurs in compound words ({連濁|れんだく}). There are many varieties depending on the dish: {二杯酢|にはいず} (vinegar + soy sauce), {三杯酢|さんばいず} (vinegar + soy sauce + mirin), {寿司酢|すしず} (sushi vinegar), etc.

TYPES:
- {二杯酢|にはいず}: two-part vinegar (vinegar + soy sauce)
- {三杯酢|さんばいず}: three-part vinegar (vinegar + soy sauce + mirin)
- {寿司酢|すしず}: sushi vinegar (vinegar + sugar + salt)
- {甘酢|あまず}: sweet vinegar
